## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `c2b0e3ad1b7bc4170352cda80eb5953676715c63`
Local-runs: none
Scope: docs/adr/0070-package-first-authoring.md + packages/runtime/src/domains/packages.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/package-writability.ts, packages/spec/src/api/package-api-assembled.zod.ts, packages/objectql/src/registry.ts, packages/triggers/trigger-record-change/src/record-change-trigger.ts, packages/core/src/artifact-packages.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts, packages/runtime/src/domains/packages-disable-app-module.test.ts, content/docs/deployment/marketplace-handbook.mdx, docs/adr/0146-studio-designs-setup-administers-one-editor-per-item-paired-customize-package.md, docs/adr/0141-inter-app-dependency-declared-checked-before-install.md (all read on `main` at `ea1751be`, which carries PR #28308's merge `7abe151b`)

Inputs read: card #28285 (body, triage, unblock, claim, dev report `6545434096`); parent #28117 (ruling record in the body, scope addendum `6523684730`, decision letter `6538936519`, landing record, director batch note); PR #28430 body, file list, net diff against `main` and the check-runs on the head; PR #28308 (merged, file list); issue #28318 (the `disableable` key) and #28118 (the Console half). The dispatch order was read for the seat's rulings only; nothing below rests on its conclusions.

### ① Derived judgments

- **Accept set: nothing moves.** One file, `docs/adr/0070-package-first-authoring.md`, +3/−1. No `packages/spec/src/**`, no runtime, no skills, no changeset. The diff publishes no key, refusal or served shape; the behaviour it records is already on `main` from PR #28308 (`7abe151b`), which carried its own `yes (widening)`. Right.
- **Governed face: one hit.** `docs/adr/**` is the governed rules text, so the PR is Tier H and the review is owed at `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`. The PR is draft with no auto-merge and no readiness, as the Tier H line requires. Right.
- **Public surface of the ADR: two edits, both additive.** (a) A dated `· **Amended** (…)` pointer appended to the Status line, after ADR-0146's `Superseded in part` pointer, leaving that pointer and its "D1, D2, D4 and D6 stand" sentence untouched. (b) One blockquote `> **Amended … —** …` note under D2, after D2's predicate sentence and before D3's heading. D1, D3–D6, Consequences, Open questions and Rollout are untouched. Right.
- **Symbol anchors: five new, all resolve on `main`.** `packages/runtime/src/domains/packages.ts#isDisableableAppModule` (module-level function), `packages/metadata-protocol/src/package-writability.ts#isWritablePackage` (exported), `packages/spec/src/api/package-api-assembled.zod.ts#SERVED_ROW_VERDICTS` (module const), `packages/objectql/src/registry.ts#applyNavContributions` (public method), `packages/triggers/trigger-record-change/src/record-change-trigger.ts#RecordChangeTrigger` (exported class). Each declaration found by reading the file; the "Lint & Repo Gates" check-run on the head is green. Right.
- **Issue links:** `#28117` and PR `#28308` as absolute GitHub links, the form the Status-line precedents use (ADR-0035, ADR-0043). Right.

### ② Semver level

- `skip-changeset` is stored on the PR with `documentation` and `size/xs`; `docs/adr/**` publishes nothing, so no changeset is owed. Right.
- Body declarations: `Clause-②: no` (prose only, no narrowing arm) and `Metadata-protocol: none` (`packages/spec` untouched). Both match the diff.
- Check-runs on the head at this read: Lint & Repo Gates, Test UI, Dogfood Regression Gate, Plan Test Core shards, Auto Label all green; `Test Core (1/8)` still in progress, nothing red. The landing seat reads it green before the Tier H hand-off; a docs-only tree cannot have changed its inputs.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Author is `objectstack-fleet[bot]` (the relay); no human login to name.
- Dev report `6545434096`: `open_questions: []`. One `out_of_scope_findings` entry, carrier #28117: the in-process `ctx.api` question waits on decision letter `6538936519`, and the note's last sentence is the one to amend if the maintainer rules B or C. **Answered:** the amendment records that question as *not decided here* and names the letter; #28117 is open with `needs-user-decision` and is in the director's batch #433. Nothing in the ADR text forecloses either outcome; a later ruling needs one sentence changed, exactly where the dev says.
- Deviations listed (model-free trailers, no assignees, unshallowed checkout) touch process only, not the text. The PR body's "form ADR-0087 and ADR-0005 use" claim is checked under ④ and holds.
- No flag or question is left unanswered or escalated.

### ④ Design judgment

**The amendment note, sentence by sentence against `main`.**

1. *Ruling and its three defaults* (suite as one artifact, admin switches per environment, "disabled" has one meaning: hidden, refused on the data plane, data kept) — verbatim from the #28117 ruling record. Holds.
2. *"Read-only above means may not be authored into; it does not mean may not be switched off."* — D2's own text says "Read-only. New items may not be authored into them", and `isWritablePackage`'s doc and `isDisableableAppModule`'s doc both spell `writable` as "may author into". Holds.
3. *The door reads one exemption before the writability check, `isDisableableAppModule`.* — `PATCH /packages/:id/disable` on `main` runs `isDisableablePackage(qlService, id) ? null : requireWritablePackage(deps, qlService, id, 'disable')`, and `isDisableablePackage` evaluates `isDisableableAppModule` first, then `isWritablePackage`. Holds; the note names `isDisableablePackage` indirectly as "the predicate the door asks" in the served-verdict sentence, so a reader reaches the real symbol.
4. *The tie, as shipped:* `manifest.type === 'module'`; `manifest.dependencies` directly naming a package installed here whose `manifest.type === 'app'`; own `manifest.scope` not `system`/`cloud`. — `isDisableableAppModule` reads exactly these three from the registry row (`declaredDependencyIds` returns the keys of the `dependencies` record, ADR-0141 D1's declaration, so "directly" is right; "installed here" is `registry.getPackage(dependency)` answering a row; the scope list is `READ_ONLY_PACKAGE_SCOPES`). The self-exclusion `dependency !== id` is an implementation guard the note need not state. "Both install paths leave it on the registry row" is pinned in `packages-disable-app-module.test.ts` for `code` and `marketplace`. Holds.
5. *"Everything else answers the door as before."* — the door falls through to `requireWritablePackage` for the app itself, plugins, drivers, orphan modules and platform-scope modules; the enable door is unchanged. Holds.
6. *`isWritablePackage` unchanged; edit, publish, revert, delete and overwrite still `422 WRITABLE_PACKAGE_REQUIRED`.* — `package-writability.ts` is not in PR #28308's file list and reads as before; every other package door (`install`/overwrite, `publish`, `revert`, `adopt`, `edit`, `delete`) asks `requireWritablePackage` alone. Holds.
7. *The verdict is served beside it as `disableable`, computed by the predicate the door asks.* — `withDisableableVerdict` calls `isDisableablePackage`; `SERVED_ROW_VERDICTS` declares `disableable` beside `writable` and forbids deriving one from the other. Holds.
8. *While disabled: `404 OBJECT_PACKAGE_DISABLED` on the data plane and by-name reads; the nav fold drops its contributions; record-change flows withheld for in-process writes too.* — `assertObjectRegistered` in `protocol.ts` and the by-name read answer that code; `applyNavContributions` skips a contribution whose `packageId` is disabled, per read, before the group lookup; `RecordChangeTrigger` returns before dispatch when `registry.isObjectPackageDisabled(written)` is true, per write. "Too" is right: a data-plane write never reaches the trigger (it is refused first), so the withholding is what the in-process path meets. Holds.
9. *Enable restores all three; the data was never touched.* — all three checks are asked per request and nothing is cached or deleted; the test pins the restore. Holds.
10. *Not decided here: in-process `ctx.api` access; today served, pinned and documented; with the maintainer as letter `6538936519`.* — pinned in `packages-disable-app-module.test.ts` (the addendum-6523684730 describe block), documented in `marketplace-handbook.mdx` ("What your app's own code meets"), and the letter is open on #28117. The note takes no side. Holds, and it is the sentence the order forbade from being settled.

**ADR-0146 supersession.** Its supersede table row for ADR-0070 names D3 (select-or-create a base first) and D5 (retire the stopgaps) for the paired case only, and its pointer on ADR-0070's Status line says "D1, D2, D4 and D6 stand". D2 is not superseded, so an amendment under D2 sits beside ADR-0146. Its D3 pair package (a base's customize package) is a project-scope writable base, never a `type: module`, so the exemption does not reach it; ADR-0141's open item on dependents of a disabled package is not claimed. No conflict.

**Status-line form.** The repo marks an amendment on the Status line as `· **Amended** (date, #card — clause)` (ADR-0035, ADR-0043, ADR-0045, ADR-0017) and in the body as a dated `> **Amended … —** …` blockquote (ADR-0005, ADR-0035, ADR-0048, ADR-0087); ADR-0146's "Status-line pointers" section fixes the Status line as the one place for the pointer. The PR follows both; the pointer says which clause changed and where the note is, and the generated index is reported current.

**First consumers, and does the text help them.** (a) #28118, the Console half (Packages page Enable/Disable on module rows): the note names `disableable` as the served key and the spec symbol, and says `writable` stays `false` for a module, which is the one mistake that page could make. (b) A client refused at the disable door: the `422` body's `docs:` field points at this ADR, and the note is now the sentence telling them which packages the door accepts. (c) The HotCRM tolerance card and any later ADR PR after letter `6538936519`: the last sentence is the exact place to amend. Execution plan: none owed; the code shipped first and the record follows it, as the card required.

**Findings.**

- *should-fix* — the Status-line pointer reads "the maintainer's ruling of 2026-10-30, 「大包 + 设置里启用模块」, then 「同意」". On #28117's dated thread the first phrase is the maintainer's 2026-10-29 direction and 「同意」 is the 2026-10-30 ruling. Item 6 of the card spells it the same way, so the date is the ruling's and not wrong, but "then" invites a reader to put both on one day. A later touch could read "…the maintainer's direction 「大包 + 设置里启用模块」 and ruling 「同意」 of 2026-10-30". Not blocking: the note cites #28117, where the thread is quoted with its dates.
- No must-fix. Nothing in the amendment claims a behaviour `main` does not carry, overstates the in-process question, or reaches a clause ADR-0146 superseded.

**VERDICT: PASS**
